name: Pulse band (our own wearable)
what: A screenless band with the Pulse logo: heart rate, HRV, sleep and blood oxygen, linked to the Pulse app.

name: Face skin analyzer
what: Photographs the face to show spots, pores and wrinkles.
faq: Is a $2,000 Chinese one as good as the $7,000+ VISIA?
The photos can be close. VISIA's edge is its skin-comparison database and US service. Ask for a side-by-side demo on your own face, then compare the reports.
Can we use it on members?
Yes, as a photo and education tool. Never call the result a diagnosis.
Any hidden costs?
Ask if the software needs a yearly license or a Chinese server, and what a replacement camera costs.

name: 3D body scanner
what: Rotating scan of body shape for the monthly re-scan.
faq: Do members' scans leave the building?
Ask where scans are stored. Health data on a Chinese server is a problem for a US clinic. Best: data on our own computer or a US server.
Is there a monthly fee?
Fit3D charges about $100 a month. Ask if Visbody's software is a subscription.
How much room does it need?
Ask for the floor space, ceiling height and weight limit of the turntable.

name: Handheld heart ultrasound
what: Quick heart look when a scan flags something. Chinese brand, buy from its US dealer.
faq: Why not buy it straight from China?
Warranty, service and the FDA paperwork run through the US office. A direct import can be held at customs.
Which probe do we need for the heart?
A cardiac (phased-array) probe. In Chinese: 相控阵探头 (xiàngkòngzhèn tàntóu).
Who is allowed to scan?
Whoever the medical director approves. Check before buying.

name: IV recliners (4)
what: Reclining chairs for the IV lounge.
faq: Electric or manual?
Electric needs a UL or ETL mark. Manual skips that and costs less.
What matters for cleaning?
Wipeable medical vinyl, few seams, removable arm pads.
What else to ask?
Weight limit, lie-flat position (if someone faints), and locking wheels.

name: Medical fridge with alarm
what: Keeps IV vitamins and Botox cold. Buy the US 115V model from a US dealer.
faq: Why not import one?
Same price as the US dealer, and the US model is already 115V and listed. No reason to import.
What makes it 'medical'?
A digital temperature log and an alarm. Ask for a model that meets CDC vaccine-storage guidance.

name: Saunas
what: Traditional and infrared rooms for the thermal floor.
faq: What's the biggest risk?
The heater and controls. Without a UL or ETL listing, the NJ inspector won't sign off.
Can we buy just the room from China?
Often the smart move: a Chinese wooden cabin with a US-listed heater and controls. Ask if they'll sell the cabin without the heater.
How long until it arrives?
Usually 30–60 days to build plus 30–40 days by sea. Confirm in writing.

name: Hydro pools and spa
what: Two 7×10 ft hydro pools and the round spa. NJ health department must approve the plans.
faq: What do the NJ rules need?
Health department plan approval for a spa used by the public, and pool pumps and filters usually need NSF/ANSI 50 for public pools.
Who installs and repairs it?
Ask if they have a US installer or service partner. If not, find one before ordering.
What else to ask?
The heater and pump wattage, and whether every electrical part is UL or ETL listed.

name: Cold plunge chillers
what: Chillers and tubs for the four cold plunges.
faq: What has to be certified?
The chiller (it's electrical): UL or ETL. Ask how the water is kept clean (ozone, UV, filter).
Do they make for US brands?
Ask which ones, then Harris checks it on ImportYeti (US customs records).
What's the running cost?
Ask the power draw in watts and the noise level.

name: Red light bed
what: Full-body LED bed. Phase 2. Only with a real FDA number.
faq: Is it a medical device?
Light beds sold for wrinkles or pain need an FDA 510(k). Without a K-number, it's a no for 510 Summit.
What power does it need?
Big beds draw a lot. Ask the watts and whether it needs a 240V circuit.
How long do the lights last?
Ask the LED lifetime in hours and the price of a replacement panel.

name: Compression boots
what: Leg recovery for the lounge and recovery room.
faq: Can we sell recovery with these?
Yes, for recovery and wellness. Medical claims (swelling, clots) need FDA clearance.
What wears out?
The leg sleeves. Ask the price of spare sleeves and how they're cleaned.

name: Treatment and blood-draw chairs
faq: Electric or manual?
Electric needs a UL or ETL mark. Manual skips that.
What makes a good blood-draw chair?
Arms that lock, can tip back if someone faints, wipeable vinyl.

name: Lockers, towel warmers, lighting
zh: 更衣柜 / 毛巾加热柜 / 灯具
what: The look Carissa designs. She approves finishes first.
faq: How do we avoid surprises?
Get samples of every finish first. Carissa approves before anything is ordered.
What needs certificates?
Anything that plugs in (UL or ETL), and fire ratings for lockers and fabrics.
